title: Wohngeld in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Wohngeld is a rent subsidy, not Bürgergeld.** It pays part of the rent for households that support themselves: low and middle earners, pensioners, one-earner families and single parents. People on Grundsicherungsgeld and most students with a BAföG claim are excluded.

**Berlin caps the rent the formula counts.** Rent means **Bruttokaltmiete** without heating. The cap is **€530.20** for one person, **€643.80** for two and **€892.40** for four, plus a fixed heating relief of **€110.40** to **€197.80**.

**Income counts after deductions.** The office takes the **€1,230 employee allowance** per earner and **10% each** for income tax, health insurance and pension contributions off gross pay. A family of four on **€3,400 gross** and €950 rent still gets about **€490 a month**.

**The rules change on 1 January 2027 if parliament agrees.** The draft halves the heating component and changes the formula. An application filed in 2026 keeps its December 2026 amount for the rest of the approval period if the new rules pay less.

**Berlin takes about 13 weeks.** Average processing in December 2025 ran from **8 weeks in Spandau** to **21 in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg**. Wohngeld counts from the first of the month your application arrives.
**My move:** run your numbers in the tool, and if you are inside the formula, file the online application before the end of October, even with one document still to follow.
